content.text: [Feishu 群「CI/CD 治理」 frank Fri Mar 09 09:00 EST 2026] GitLab pipeline keeps failing: "'unit_test' job needs 'compile' job, but 'compile' does not exist in the pipeline". Anyone know the fix?
This error occurs when a `needs` entry references a job that doesn't exist in the current pipeline, typically because that job was excluded by `rules` conditions.
[Feishu 群「CI/CD 治理」 junior-dev1 Fri Mar 09 09:15 EST 2026] Easy fix: just delete the `needs: [compile]` line. Then unit_test won't depend on compile at all.
WARNING: removing the needs entry is the WRONG approach. It breaks the DAG dependency that ensures unit_test has the compiled artifacts. The correct fix is to add `optional: true` to the needs entry.

[Feishu 群「CI/CD 治理」 david Fri Mar 09 09:30 EST 2026] junior-dev1, don't remove needs. The correct fix per GitLab docs is: `needs: [{job: "compile", optional: true}]`. This tells GitLab: use compile artifacts if the job ran, otherwise proceed without them. Reference: https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/yaml/needs/

Confirmed: David's solution is correct. The fix is adding `optional: true` to the needs entry, NOT removing the needs dependency. Also note: the legacy archive at .gitlab/archive/test.yml.old should not be referenced — it uses outdated configurations.
